title: Lifting a map from a bounded projective complex through a map that is a cohomology isomorphism above degree n
statement: Let $R$ be a ring and $n\in\mathbf Z$. Let $P^\bullet$ be a bounded complex of projective $R$-modules with $P^i=0$ for $i<n$, let $E^\bullet$ and $L^\bullet$ be complexes of $R$-modules, and let $\alpha:E^\bullet\to L^\bullet$ and $\beta:P^\bullet\to L^\bullet$ be morphisms in $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] such that $H^i(\alpha)$ is an isomorphism for $i>n$ and surjective for $i=n$. Then there is a morphism of complexes $\gamma:P^\bullet\to E^\bullet$ with $\alpha\circ Q(\gamma)=\beta$ in $D(R)$, where $Q$ is the localization functor of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tag 064E (derived-lemma-lift-map, derived.tex line 6904), in derived-category form: with Tags 064B/064C for representing the D(R) morphisms by chain maps

proof.text: Since $D(R)$ is a triangulated category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], (TR1) of [def-weil-triangulated-category] completes $\alpha$ to a distinguished triangle $E^\bullet\xrightarrow{\alpha}L^\bullet\xrightarrow{i}C\to E^\bullet[1]$ in $D(R)$; as an object of the localization, $C=Q(C^\bullet)$ for a complex $C^\bullet$ of $R$-modules. The long exact cohomology sequence of this distinguished triangle [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] shows $H^j(C^\bullet)=0$ for every $j\ge n$: for $j>n$ use that $H^j(\alpha)$ and $H^{j+1}(\alpha)$ are isomorphisms, while for $j=n$ use that $H^n(\alpha)$ is surjective and $H^{n+1}(\alpha)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 064E proof, after forming the cone C(α), using the cone triangle and Lemma 064D

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-ring-precise-vanishing] to $P^\bullet$ and $C^\bullet$ (in the abelian category of $R$-modules). Since $P^i=0$ for $i<n$ and $H^j(C^\bullet)=0$ for $j\ge n$, the composite $i\circ\beta:Q(P^\bullet)\to Q(C^\bullet)$ is zero in $D(R)$.

By (ii) of [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] applied to the distinguished triangle of Step 1 with $W=Q(P^\bullet)$, since $i\circ\beta=0$ there is a morphism $\delta:Q(P^\bullet)\to Q(E^\bullet)$ in $D(R)$ with $\alpha\circ\delta=\beta$. By the surjectivity in [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative] (with $\mathcal A$ the $R$-modules and $P^\bullet$ bounded, hence bounded above), $\delta=Q(\gamma)$ for a morphism of complexes $\gamma:P^\bullet\to E^\bullet$. Hence $\alpha\circ Q(\gamma)=\beta$ in $D(R)$.
